newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks inch lower in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks inch lower in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks inched lower in early Friday morning trade, but brokers said the market was likely to experience only a short bout of profit-taking before forging to higher levels.

"This is just a bit of profit-taking. We went up too much too fast yesterday," said Steven Cheng, associate director at Lippo Securities. "It is going to be a minor correction, not even a correction, a pullback of not more than 100 points."
The Hang Seng Index was just three points lower at 16,361 after 30 minutes of trade on heavy turnover of HK$4.87 billion.
"The background music is still good," said Cheng, indicating Hong Kong's low interest rate looked set to continue and the currency was one of the most stable in the region.
Foreign exchange traders said the Hong Kong dollar has remained relatively steady in the past eight weeks at around HK$7.743 to the U.S. dollar.

Trading in Hang Seng Index futures was also sending positive signals to the cash market, brokers said. The August contract was trading just 30 points higher at 16,465 but that represented about a 100-point premium to spot.

"There aren't that many people who are bearish," said Alistair Candlish, managing director of trading and derivatives at Indosuez W.I Carr Securities. "The (futures) market is trading in line with the cash market."
"It is a very friendly atmosphere," Candlish added.
Properties outperformed the index and H shares outperformed all blue chip sectors.
Sun Hung Kai Properties was the most actively traded rising HK$3.25 to HK$100.50 on trade of HK$610 million. Cheung Kong jumped HK$1.25 to HK$87.25.

The H share index was trading 1.5 percent higher. Among the most actively traded were Shanghai Hai Xing Shipping which added HK$0.25 to trade at HK$5.45, Tianjin Bohai which leaped to a new high of HK$1.72, then eased to trade HK$0.25 or 18 percent higher at HK$1.64.
Maanshan Iron soared to a new high of HK$2.45 before falling back to trade HK$0.175 higher at HK$2.275.
Brokers said some of the biggest H share movers were laggards in previous China play rallies, while others were the target to red-chip style restructuring and asset injections.
Red chip Beijing Enterprise was trading HK$1.95 higher at HK$51.25 on asset injections rumours, brokers said.
